_comment: Disposition of every Astro-owned preference, for the Astro Next baseline (issue #6).
The preference NAMES are not written here. They are parsed out of the
committed patch stack by tools/baseline/make_profile_fixtures.py, because a
hand-written list of pref names is a second copy of the registry that nothing
keeps in sync, and the first rename makes it describe a browser that no longer
exists.
What cannot be parsed is the JUDGEMENT: whether a preference is part of the
reproducible legacy baseline, or is candidate future work that exists only in
somebody's working tree. That is what this file holds -- the same split, and
for the same reason, as patch-dispositions.json beside it.
status:
legacy-baseline
Registered by the COMMITTED patch stack. It is present in the fixtures
under test/astro-next/fixtures/, and a clean checkout regenerates those
fixtures byte for byte.
observed-local-only
Registered ONLY in a working-tree copy of a patch, never at HEAD, and
therefore NOT part of the baseline. Recorded here so the observation is
not lost, and deliberately kept OUT of the fixtures: a fixture a clean
checkout cannot regenerate is worse than a missing one, because it makes
--verify fail for everybody except the machine that produced it.
These are candidate future preferences. The issue named in owner_issue
decides whether each one ships, under what name, and with what default;
when it does, the work lands as a committed patch change and the entry
here is reclassified to legacy-baseline (or deleted).
THE JOIN IS STRICT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what stops this file rotting:
* a preference the committed patches register with no entry here  -> fails
* a preference the committed patches register whose entry says
observed-local-only                                              -> fails
* an entry marked legacy-baseline that the committed patches do not
register                                                         -> fails
* an entry marked observed-local-only that the committed patches DO
register                                                         -> fails
The last one is the load-bearing direction. The day the local preference work
is committed, every entry below flips from true to false at once, and the join
fails naming each one -- so this file has to be brought up to date rather than
quietly becoming a false statement about the repository. A note in prose could
not do that.
observed_in is the patch whose working-tree copy registers the preference. It
is checked against the patch list the tool parses, so a typo names nothing
rather than pointing nowhere.

oxy.access_token.purpose: Oxy account access token, mirrored into the profile from the token store.

oxy.refresh_token.purpose: Oxy account refresh token, mirrored into the profile from the token store.

oxy.session_id.purpose: Identifier of the signed-in Oxy session.

oxy.username.purpose: Signed-in Oxy account handle, as displayed in the browser UI.

oxy.user_avatar.purpose: Avatar file id for the signed-in Oxy account.

oxy.token_expiry.purpose: Expiry of the stored access token.

oxy.adblock.enabled.purpose: Master switch for the ad blocker.

oxy.adblock.site_overrides.purpose: Per-site ad blocker exceptions. Only disabled sites are stored; re-enabling a site removes its key rather than storing true.

oxy.adblock.custom_rules.purpose: User-authored filter rules, one per line, in Adblock Plus syntax.

astro.ntp_show_weather.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: weather.

astro.ntp_show_clock.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: clock.

astro.ntp_show_quick_links.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: quick links.

astro.ntp_show_notes.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: notes.

astro.ntp_show_sites.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: most-visited sites.

astro.ntp_show_discover.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: discover feed.

astro.ntp_show_alia.purpose: New Tab Page widget visibility: Alia entry point.

oxy.adblock.lifetime_blocked_count.purpose: Cumulative count of requests the ad blocker has blocked, for the shield UI.

astro.theme.preset.purpose: The active Bloom colour preset, by name. Paints the native browser UI through ui/astro_color_mixer.cc and every astro:// page through astro_theme.mojom, so both read one stored value and cannot drift. Deliberately paired with upstream's browser.theme.color_scheme2 for light/dark rather than adding a second Astro pref for it.
